mixed_block.assertion: Only the fully bound+committed slot used its durable score before reconciliation; the bound-but-uncommitted slot became usable only after exact COMMIT.

torn_commit_frame.assertion: No torn COMMIT prefix entered scientific evidence.

random_fuzz.assertion: Across all generated mixtures, every noncompliant planned slot scored exactly 1 and audited block_score was never more optimistic (lower) than the legacy SLOT-accepting view.

measurement_validity_rules: A lower-level SLOT event is not scientific evidence under the reservation-aware contract merely because the historical atomic journal accepted it.
A planned slot is score-bearing only after durable RESERVE, exact attempt binding inside the canonical SLOT event, and durable COMMIT referencing that exact SLOT event digest.
Bound SLOT without COMMIT is recoverable bookkeeping, not yet compliant scientific evidence; before reconciliation it remains failure=1.
Missing reservation with no SLOT is an ordinary never-launched failure=1, while a SLOT without reservation is a bypass and is also failure=1.
Dirty/torn main or reservation-ledger tails must be repaired/quarantined before audit; the auditor never reasons past a torn prefix.
The auditor is active-block only and does not reinterpret already closed historical blocks.
known_limitations: This validation used contract-faithful injected atomic/reservation codecs because the repository sibling files are not mounted in the local Python runtime.

The auditor computes the compliant row but does not yet replace the historical CLOSE/replay semantics; a next-version CLOSE wrapper must persist the compliance row/digest so future replay cannot re-admit bypass SLOTs.
Multi-process writer fencing is not addressed here.
next_action: Integrate the auditor into a new compliance-aware CLOSE/replay wrapper that persists compliance_digest + compliant closed row and rebuilds reporter state from that row, then crash-inject CLOSE persistence so unbound/bypass SLOTs can never reappear after restart.
